title: Continental Genesis & the Recent-Sequence Cascade — Why Dry Land Exists, and Its Coupled Flood→Glaciation→Atlantic-Opening Relaxation
abstract: Two coupled geophysics papers under one jamming kernel. PART I (Continental Genesis) asks why a two-tier crust — dry continents above deep ocean basins — exists at all, and derives it from a buoyancy gate, a wet partial-melting granite step, an isostatic-compensation law, and an area-fraction percolation attractor on a ~6-connected plate network (closing the CG-39 connectivity gap), with no fitted parameter. PART II (Recent-Sequence Cascade) reads one relaxation of the same engine three ways — a flood, a glaciation, and the opening of the Atlantic — as a single coupled instance: void-suction unjamming releases jammed State-4 water (S0), a freshwater lid drives anoxia and dual-redox evaporite pathways, and a magnitude-ratio discriminator with an occurrence cap makes the chain falsifiable. Both parts inherit the kernel (c²=B/ρ, R19), the DNA γ atlas, and the rotor-inflow module from the physics, geodynamics, geochronology, fluid-dynamics, and dna volumes; both keep a chronology firewall.
